subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` `started` mean the user turn is durable or visibly progressing before ACK, or is the current UI-only pending/history preservation the intended contract?
rationale: The remaining fix changes the Gateway send boundary and transcript ownership semantics, which affects latency, duplicate suppression, rollover, and message-delivery behavior beyond a narrow UI patch.

options.title: Port durable Gateway contract
options.body: Route WebChat user-turn durability through the current recorder/session boundary before or at ACK, with coverage for busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure paths.

options.title: Keep UI-only mitigation
options.body: Treat `started` as admission only and close or narrow the Gateway persistence work, accepting that durability remains runtime-owned after ACK.

options.title: Require live current-main repro first
options.body: Pause code changes until maintainers or a contributor captures a current-main live reproduction that proves the remaining Gateway gap still manifests for users.

recommendation.title: Port durable Gateway contract
recommendation.body: Route WebChat user-turn durability through the current recorder/session boundary before or at ACK, with coverage for busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on the user-turn transcript recorder and Gateway persistence boundary they most directly touched.
